Deprecate unused Scope-related methods (#7255)

* Deprecate ObservationView.getEnclosingScope()

getEnclosingScope() was added in 1.10.6 (PR #3731) so that
ObservationThreadLocalAccessor.restore(Observation) could obtain the
observation's enclosing scope and call makeCurrent() before setValue().

In 1.10.x (PR #3831, NullObservation) the restore logic was changed to
use the registry's current scope and getPreviousObservationScope()
instead. Since then, getEnclosingScope() has not been used by any
production code; the only remaining callers are tests in
ObservationThreadLocalAccessorTests.

Deprecating the method is a first step toward removing it and the
lastScope field in SimpleObservation, which will reduce per-observation
overhead (ConcurrentHashMap field and scope bookkeeping on open/close).

* Deprecate Scope.makeCurrent()

makeCurrent() was added in 1.10.6 (PR #3731) so that
ObservationThreadLocalAccessor.restore(Observation) could re-apply an
observation's scope when restoring: it called value.getEnclosingScope()
then enclosingScope.makeCurrent() before setValue(value).

In 1.10.x (PR #3831, NullObservation) the restore logic was changed to
use the registry's current scope and closeCurrentScope() instead.
Since then, makeCurrent() has not been used by any production code; the
only remaining caller is the test CurrentObservationTest.nestedScopes_makeCurrent().

Deprecating the method aligns with the getEnclosingScope() deprecation
and allows future removal of the scope-rebuild logic in SimpleScope that
exists only to support makeCurrent().

* Deprecate Scope.reset() and ObservationHandler.onScopeReset()

Scope.reset() was used by ObservationThreadLocalAccessor until 1.10.x
(PR #3831, NullObservation). That flow called reset() to clear thread
locals before making another scope current. After #3831, OTLA uses
closeCurrentScope() with scope.close() instead, so Scope.reset() is no
longer used by any production code; the only remaining caller is
ObservationValidatorTests.scopeResetAfterStopShouldBeValid().

ObservationHandler.onScopeReset(Context) is only invoked when
Scope.reset() or Scope.makeCurrent() runs. Both are now deprecated
and unused in production, so the callback is deprecated as well.
Handlers should use onScopeClosed for cleanup when a scope is closed.

Deprecating these aligns with deprecating getEnclosingScope() and Scope.makeCurrent() and allows future removal of the reset/makeCurrent-related code paths.

Add Scope closing validation to ObservationValidator (#7253)

Add two new opt-in validation capabilities for TestObservationRegistry:

- SCOPES_SHOULD_BE_CLOSED_IN_REVERSE_ORDER_OF_OPENING: Validates that
  scopes are closed in LIFO order. If scope A is opened then scope B,
  scope B must be closed before scope A.

- SCOPES_SHOULD_BE_OPENED_AND_CLOSED_ON_THE_SAME_THREAD: Validates that
  a scope is closed on the same thread it was opened on.

Both validations are opt-in via the TestObservationRegistryBuilder to
avoid breaking existing tests in reactive contexts where scope handling
may follow different patterns.

Closes gh-6329

Mark nullability on Meter.match (#7481)

Removes the @NullUnmarked workaround on Meter.match and expresses the nullability contract with JSpecify.

match returns whatever the selected visitor returns, so the result type has to allow null when a visitor returns null. Switched the type parameter to <T extends @Nullable Object>; the visitor functions themselves stay non-null.

Updated test call sites that passed null for unused visitors to pass x -> null instead, since Function params are no longer nullable. Added a test for the match-returns-null case.

Closes gh-6408

Skip registering JCache meters when statistics are not enabled (#7562)

* Skip registering JCache meters when statistics are not enabled

When a JCache cache is bound without statistics enabled, the registered
meters silently report zero, which is hard to diagnose. Detect this case
via CompleteConfiguration#isStatisticsEnabled() and skip registering the
stats-dependent meters; log a warning explaining how to enable
statistics. This mirrors what was done for Caffeine in gh-5402 and
gh-5409.

If the JCache provider does not expose CompleteConfiguration (the
configuration is null or getConfiguration() throws
IllegalArgumentException), assume statistics are enabled to avoid a
false-positive warning.

See gh-5066.

Signed-off-by: jewoodev <jewoos15@naver.com>

* Document that JCache statistics toggles are not tracked

JCacheMetrics checks whether statistics are enabled at construction time.
Runtime toggles via CacheManager#enableStatistics(...) are intentionally
not tracked, so metrics need to be rebound if statistics are enabled later.

Signed-off-by: jewoodev <jewoos15@naver.com>

Optimize PrometheusMeterRegistry and MicrometerCollector snapshot collection (#7802)

Refactor `PrometheusMeterRegistry` and `MicrometerCollector` to improve code readability/maintainability and minimize per-scrape memory allocation and CPU overhead:

- Construct `MeterContext` (pre-formatted tag keys, tag values, and help text) and `Labels` once at meter registration time instead of re-evaluating them on every scrape request.
- Simplify `MicrometerCollector` by removing intermediate `Child` and `Family` wrapper abstractions, streaming native Prometheus Client 1.x `MetricFamilyDescriptor` and `DataPointSnapshot` instances directly.
- Cache and reuse `MetricFamilyDescriptor` objects per family in a pre-sized map within `MicrometerCollector`.
- Pre-size temporary maps and snapshot lists in `collect()` to eliminate array resizing and reduce garbage collector pressure during scrapes.

Benchmark results on 500 meters:
- `collect()` allocation reduced by -89.7% (185.4 KB → 18.59 KB / scrape)
- `collect()` execution time improved by ~4.2x (50.4 µs → 11.94 µs / scrape)
- Full `scrape()` allocation reduced by -64.1% (264.4 KB → 94.81 KB / scrape)

The structure of the code is hopefully easier to follow and reason about now. Additional improvements still exist, but this is a first refactor.

Fix StatsdMeterRegistry client readiness check in tests (#7874)

When checking if the StatsdMeterRegistry client is ready before
emitting metrics in tests, the connection swap starts as null while
the background connection is being established.

Checking `!isDisposed()` on a null connection incorrectly evaluated to
ready immediately in `TelegrafStatsdLineBuilderIntegrationTest`, causing
metrics to be dropped and leading to flaky test failures.

This updates the test helpers to check readiness positively (`isClientReady`),
verifying that the connection is both non-null and not disposed.

Skip registering Hazelcast meters when statistics are not enabled (#7568)

Follow-up to gh-5402, gh-5409, and gh-7562 for HazelcastCacheMetrics.
When a Hazelcast `IMap` is bound without statistics enabled, the
registered meters silently report zero, which is hard to diagnose.
This change detects the stats-disabled state via
`MapConfig#isStatisticsEnabled()`, logs a warning explaining how to
enable statistics, and skips registering every stats-dependent meter,
including `cache.size` because it reads
`LocalMapStats#getOwnedEntryCount()` and is meaningless once
statistics are disabled.

See gh-5066

* Use Hazelcast `Config` to detect statistics

Avoid relying on Hazelcast internal SPI classes to inspect map
configuration. Add `Config`-based overloads that use the public API while
preserving the behavior of existing overloads.

Wait for InfluxDB readiness in TelegrafStatsdLineBuilderIntegrationTest (#7909)

In InfluxDB 2.x, the `/ping` endpoint responds with 204 as soon as the
HTTP engine starts listening, before the automated setup creates the
organization, bucket, and authentication token.

This updates the InfluxDB container wait strategy to check `GET /ready`
(200), ensuring the database has completed initial setup before tests
start emitting metrics. Also increases the assertion timeout to 10
seconds for CI stability.

Make active LTT opt-in in DefaultMeterObservationHandler (#7944)

Deprecate existing constructors and introduce a builder that defaults to not including the active observation LongTaskTimer. Effectively switch the non-deprecated API to be opt-in to including the active Observation LongTaskTimer instead of the previous behavior of opt-out. This better signals what we now think the default behavior should be. It's unclear how much people are using the produced LongTaskTimer, if at all, and in at least Spring's web server instrumentation its usefulness is severely limited by the URI pattern not being available when the Observation is started. Hence, to avoid everyone paying the cost of the LongTaskTimer, limit it to those who intentionally want it.

Closes gh-7312

Introduce per-convention meter convention types and builder pattern (#7369)

Replace group interfaces (e.g., JvmMemoryMeterConventions) with specific
per-convention interfaces (e.g., JvmMemoryUsedMeterConvention) following
the proven ObservationConvention pattern. This resolves issues where the
OTel variant extending the Micrometer variant made the class hierarchy awkward (e.g. in Spring Boot auto-configuration), and where customizing a single meter
required implementing the entire group interface.

Each binder now has a builder with per-convention setters and an
`openTelemetryConventions()` convenience method. The binder merges extra
tags itself so conventions stay purely semantic. Each specific interface
provides a static of() factory for inline custom implementations.

Group interfaces and their implementations are deprecated in favor of
the new per-convention types and builders.

Remove inheritance from MeterConvention on the specific per-convention
interfaces. Conventions without runtime context now define a parameterless
default getTags() method, avoiding passing null at call sites, while
contextual conventions accept their specific context type.

Deprecate MeterConvention and SimpleMeterConvention in favor of the
specific per-convention interfaces.

Explain in JavaDocs across the 4 binder builders and in the JVM reference
documentation that openTelemetryConventions() may configure additional
conventions in future minor releases as new stable OpenTelemetry conventions
become available and supported. If strict metric stability across library
upgrades is required, users should configure individual conventions
explicitly.

Match HTTP/2 GlobalRequestProcessor MBean in TomcatMetrics (#7547)

When server.http2.enabled is set, Tomcat registers a second
GlobalRequestProcessor MBean per connector with an extra Upgrade key
(e.g. Upgrade="h2c") for HTTP/2 traffic. The previous
:type=GlobalRequestProcessor,name=* pattern only matches MBeans whose
key set is exactly {name}, so the HTTP/2 aggregator was silently
ignored and tomcat.global.* reflected HTTP/1.1 only.

Broaden the pattern with a trailing ',*' (mirroring the Servlet
pattern) and surface the Upgrade key as an 'upgrade' tag on the
registered meters. HTTP/1.1 series get upgrade=none so the label set
stays consistent across protocols, which lets dimensional registries
(Prometheus, etc.) keep both as separate series instead of dropping
one as a duplicate.

The same ObjectName shape is used by Tomcat's UpgradeGroupInfo
(servlet upgrades such as WebSocket), which exposes msgsSent /
msgsReceived instead of requestCount / processingTime / etc. Skip
those MBeans by discriminating on the presence of the 'requestCount'
attribute. Tomcat wraps RequestGroupInfo in a BaseModelMBean, so
MBeanServer.isInstanceOf and className comparison both fail.

Closes gh-7535
